title: Sentinel provenance label
description: The D <-> E interface contract. A caller declares, for every message it sends, whether that message is operator-authored or derived from a target the system does not control. Stream E (the gateway) validates the declaration, marks untrusted spans and records the audit trail; Stream D enforces policy on the same labels at the agent layer. Absence of a declaration is not a neutral default - it fails closed.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Changing it is an interface change and costs both streams.

spans.description: One entry per message in the request. Coverage must be complete: an undeclared message is a rejected request, because a downstream enforcer that cannot tell trusted from untrusted will assume trusted.

message_index.description: Zero-based index into the request's messages array.

trust.description: operator: authored by the system or its operators. target-derived: obtained from a scanned target, a scanner report, a fetched page, or any other source outside the system's control. When in doubt the honest answer is target-derived.

source.description: How the content was obtained, for audit and for later enforcement policy. Required when trust is target-derived.

target.description: Identity of the target the content came from - an image digest, a pinned source revision, or an origin. Required when trust is target-derived so that a later enforcer can scope its policy per target.

collected_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the content was obtained, not when the request was sent. Stale untrusted content is a different risk from fresh untrusted content.
